observation.visible_scene: A nighttime fireworks display over a calm body of water, with a low, lit horizon of city/industrial lights stretching across the middle of the frame. Several spherical firework bursts hang in the upper half of the sky: a left cluster, a center-right cluster, and a smaller burst on the far right, each composed of many glowing dots in orange and white/gold tones. Their shimmering vertical streak reflections appear in the dark water below, mirroring the same horizontal positions. A faint horizontal band of low-level sparks flickers just above the horizon throughout.
visible_changes: The main sky bursts persist across the whole excerpt and slowly expand radially while individual dots flicker, drift, and dim, rather than appearing or vanishing abruptly.

Around the middle of the clip (frames ~14-22) additional bright white/gold spherical bursts bloom and intensify (notably a white sphere at center-left and a white sphere at the right), then fade back toward orange by the later frames.
The far-right small burst changes color/brightness over time (orange early, brighter white/gold mid-clip, dimmer orange-late) while staying near the same horizontal position.
The water reflections continuously mirror the sky bursts' brightness and color changes, elongating and wavering as the surface ripples.
The horizon light band and the scattered bright points at ground level flicker and shift in intensity but keep the same overall layout.
The lit horizon and water edges stay fixed in frame position, indicating the camera is essentially static; observed motion is from the fireworks themselves (expansion/flicker), not from panning.
outside_clip_unknowns: When the bursts were first launched and whether they fully dissipate after the excerpt.
What causes the mid-clip brightening of the white bursts (a new shell detonation vs. ignition of slower-burning stars) is not shown.
The exact number of shells and their trajectories before reaching these burst positions.
uncertain_details: Small apparent vertical drift of the clusters could be genuine upward motion of the burning particles or slight camera/zoom jitter; background evidence is too weak to separate confidently.
Some faint dots near the bursts may be lingering smoke-illuminated sparks or new tiny bursts; individual identity is hard to track.
